about: Input guardrails: values that are impossible or nonsense are blocked where they are entered (block), values that are unusual but possible are warned about (warn). Every entry path uses these rules: the visual editors, the New Project wizard, imports, the command line (saengine validate) and the AI assistant. A limit with 'fromPack' takes its value from the code pack in force (the code's own limit); every other number here is an SAEngine practice sanity limit, not a code requirement. Zero and negative sizes are refused by the schemas themselves (gt=0). Lengths are in mm, stresses in MPa.

block.reason: no concrete is that weak or that strong; check the value is in MPa

warn.reason: below the design code's least f'c for structural concrete; right for blinding or lean concrete only
outside the usual range of concrete; keep it only if tests give it

block.reason: no reinforcing bar has that yield strength; check the value is in MPa
above the yield strength the design code lets the design use

warn.reason: outside the usual range of reinforcement

block.reason: no structural steel has that yield strength; check the value is in MPa

warn.reason: outside the usual range of structural steel
outside the usual range of concrete; check the value is in kg/m³
outside the usual range of concrete
outside the usual range of steel; check the value is in kg/m³
outside the usual range of masonry; check the value is in kg/m³

block.reason: no member section is that large; check the value is in mm

warn.reason: an unusually large section; check the value is in mm

block.reason: no member has that much cover; check the value is in mm

warn.reason: outside the usual cover of reinforced concrete

block.reason: the cover on both faces leaves no concrete inside the bars
not one of the bar sizes of the design code
no storey is that low or that high (a hall taller than 20 m is modelled with its intermediate levels); check the levels are in mm: most storeys are 2.8 to 4.5 m

warn.reason: an unusual storey height (most storeys are 2.8 to 4.5 m, a tall ground floor up to 6 m)

block.reason: more storeys than any building has

warn.reason: a very tall building; check the number of storeys

block.reason: grid lines that close or that far apart are a slip (the longest roof spans are about 60 m); check the positions are in mm

warn.reason: an unusual span for a building grid (most frames span 3 to 9 m)

block.reason: no beam that slender carries a floor; give it a deeper type or support it

warn.reason: shallower than usual for a floor beam (span/depth 10 to 18 in practice); the deflection check decides

block.reason: no slab that thin spans that far; give it a thicker type or add beams

warn.reason: thinner than usual for its span (short span/thickness 25 to 36 in practice); the deflection check decides

no floor carries that much live load; check the value is in kN/m² (not N/m², kg/m² or psf)

block.reason: no finish or partition allowance is that heavy; check the value is in kN/m²

block.reason: more spans than any building has

warn.reason: a very long building; check the grid

no line or point load on one member is that large; check the value is in kN/m or kN (not N/m or N)
